criterion_review.authorization: pass: current exact sender/origin/service, finite policy/session grants, invalidation and literal stale-incarnation replay
criterion_review.death: pass: authority cuts around fence/grant/publication/commit/reply, service and proxy deaths, explicit surviving-owner rejection or declared unknown outcome, fresh bootstrap and exact settlements

unsafe_review.kernel: registered fixture hooks only; unchanged public dispatch and return-state validation; one CPU, IF-clear kernel transitions; no new assembly
unsafe_review.authority: CPL3 bounded allocation-free routing/policy/resource owner; only commit changes counter; no service RW mapping to resource; exact generation identities and monotonically fenced epochs
unsafe_review.outcomes: ephemeral resource/result loss after authority death is explicitly unknown, never blindly replayed; cancel after commit does not undo effect; high-water marks survive result expiry within incarnation
unsafe_review.direct_authority: retained service endpoint survives switches but fails mandatory mutation fence; independent private RW mappings survive broker death until process teardown
unsafe_review.limits: trusted synthetic bootstrap and fixture-controlled failure schedule, no durable activation/state migration/old-code retirement, no general discovery/SDK freeze/SMP/guest UI

no native x87 debug metadata or shared-process threads

criterion_review.independent_builds: pass: three fresh public-only locked/offline Cargo roots per ISO, declared SDK 0.1.0, separate old/new service artifacts and one unchanged client
criterion_review.codec_semantics: pass: independent reference classifications, decoded field values and independently supplied producer fields; canonical bytes and paired field-swap rejection
criterion_review.compatibility_and_ownership: pass: 20 old/new service exchanges, compatible minor/echo/features, explicit major/mandatory-feature/header and payload reserved/correlation rejection; two accepted immutable moves and two rejected application messages with received handles closed
criterion_review.route_fences: pass: independent public client/service artifacts execute the full nine-incarnation route/policy matrix; delayed old epoch and retained endpoint cannot bypass the writer fence
criterion_review.runtime_hooks: pass: separate six-process ISO, full heap/slot reuse, zero/copy/reallocation failure atomicity, selected model/segmentation/libm, live FP preemption, return/panic/fallible OOM, healthy continuation and exact settlement
criterion_review.freeze_and_handoff: pass: only the exact selected contract hash freezes; distinct time/epoch domains, manual authority ownership, current provider checks and M4/M5 obligations remain explicit

unsafe_review.kernel: registered user_fixture observer and existing checked dispatcher/return-state validation; public operations cannot select return IP/selectors/privileged flags; one CPU and original deadlines/quotas
unsafe_review.register_boundary: raw pointer-bearing wrapper remains unsafe; R8/R9 zero, RAX/RDX/RCX/R11 and memory clobbers; explicit little-endian records rather than Rust layout; actual ELF and ISO payload identities checked
unsafe_review.allocator: single owning thread with no callback/signal reentry; private RW 64 KiB object, source handle closed after map; 64-byte cells/32 slots/alignment <=4096; zero before return, matching deallocation, live-allocation shutdown denied; default allocate-copy-free realloc preserves old allocation on failure
unsafe_review.fp_and_dependencies: kernel FP state access limited to eager fxsave64/fxrstor64 helpers and the audited MXCSR control reader or guarded entry snapshot; no kernel FP arithmetic; admitted user SSE2 instruction whitelist and no AVX/XSAVE/CPU dispatch or unresolved imports; selected model/segmentation/libm only execute in runtime guest
unsafe_review.authority: numeric identities and startup/checkpoint bytes confer no authority; receive outputs usable only after success; transferred handles explicitly closed on protocol rejection; existing current-session/policy/revision/deadline and writer-fence rules retained
unsafe_review.limits: trusted synthetic bootstrap; one thread/process, masked SSE exceptions, no shared-process threads/TLS/SMP, no full text/font/raster/display guest, durable policy, state migration, safe old-code retirement or general SDK release
